bulletins.title: Imposters Target Veterans with VA Benefit Promises and Upfront Fees
bulletins.summary: Scammers contact veterans via calls, texts, or direct messages claiming to represent the Department of Veterans Affairs. They charge illegal upfront fees and make deceptive promises to expedite claims or guarantee a 100% disability rating.

bulletins.title: Tech Support Scams Exploiting Microsoft Outage
bulletins.summary: Criminals take advantage of recent Microsoft service outages to contact consumers and businesses offering help to restore access. Fraudsters impersonate IT support, banks, or police to gain remote device access or steal credentials.

bulletins.title: MFA One-Time Passcode Social Engineering
bulletins.summary: Fraudsters initiate unauthorized logins to trigger genuine two-factor authentication codes to a victim's device. Posing as security representatives or customer support, they call or message to demand the passcode under the guise of stopping fraud.
phrases: verification code sent to your phone

bulletins.title: Fake FTC Websites and Agency Impersonation Calls
bulletins.summary: Scammers impersonate the Federal Trade Commission through spoofed calls and fraudulent copycat websites. They falsely tell victims they are under investigation or eligible for a cash settlement, demanding fees or personal information.
phrases: calling from the Federal Trade Commission

add_phrases: verification code sent to your phone
calling from the Federal Trade Commission

gemini_context_snippet: Watch for callers claiming to fast-track VA benefits or guarantee higher disability ratings in exchange for upfront fees. Be cautious of unsolicited calls offering IT support to fix Microsoft service outages, and never disclose one-time MFA verification passcodes to inbound callers claiming to be security representatives.
